title: My Story for You – Subjective Experiences of Illness, Life and Healthcare of Patients and Relatives
summary: People experience illness and healthcare in different ways. Their personal experiences can provide important insights into what they perceive as helpful, supportive or challenging in healthcare. In the study “My Story for You (MeiGeDi)”, adult patients and relatives are interviewed about their experiences of illness, life and healthcare. The focus is on participants’ personal stories and their experiences of healthcare. The interviews are recorded and subsequently transcribed. For scientific analysis, the interview transcripts are anonymised and analysed qualitatively. The study explores participants’ experiences and recurring themes in their narratives and considers what these may imply for person-centred and safe healthcare.
conditions: Experiences of illness, life and healthcare in the context of healthcare; not restricted to a specific disease or diagnosis.

interventions.name: Adult patients and relatives who are capable of providing informed consent participate in a narrative-oriented, semi-structured individual interview about their subjective experiences of illness, life and healthcare. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients or adult relatives with experiences in the context of healthcare; ability to understand the nature, significance and implications of study participation and to provide written informed consent independently; sufficient German language proficiency to understand the study information and consent and to participate in the interview in German; voluntary participation following written information and informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Minors; persons who are unable to provide informed consent for study participation independently; persons with insufficient German language proficiency to understand the study information and consent or to participate in the interview; persons who, at the time of recruitment or interview, are in a direct nursing, therapeutic, advisory or other professional dependency relationship with the interviewing student.
